sentences.text: JUDGMENT
Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:

sentences.text: That on 19.05.2024 at about 7.00 PM.

he was walking by the side of the Chikkanahalli road, Nandagudi hobli, Bangalore Rural District, wherein driver of the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-53-HU-2652 drove it in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from the behind and caused the accident.

In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries, he was shifted to MVJ Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for the accidental injuries and spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards his medical expenses.
Petitioner stated that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the he was hale and healthy and he is aged about 43 years and he was self employee and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent no.2 who insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and the jurisdictional police have registered the Cr.No.114/2024 against the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they have appeared through their counsels filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the vehicle belongs to respondent No.2.
They contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligence act of the petitioner.

Respondent No.2 contended that he has insured his vehicle with respondent No.1 company, the said policy was valid as on the date of the accident and the driver was having valid DL as on the date of the accident and they prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4.
Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and he examined doctor and MRO as PW-2 and 3, produced and marked 19 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 19 and they are fully cross examined.

5. Respondents have not chosen to lead their evidence after obtaining sufficient opportunity from this Tribunal, there is no material on record to show that they are prevented from appearing before this tribunal to lead their evidence.
Hence their evidence is taken as nil.
6. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.05.2024 at about 7.00 PM. he was walking on the side of the Chikkanahalli road, Nandagudi hobli, Bangalore Rural Basant Kumar vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63589495/

sentences.text: 2 District, wherein driver of the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-53-HU-2652 drove it in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from behind and caused the accident.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether respondent no.1 proves that the driver of the offending vehicle was having no valid driving license, as on the date of accident as contended in the written statement ?

3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the Negative  Issue no.3: In Partly Affirmative  Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 9. Issue No.1 to 3:- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

He has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, IMV, wound certificate,
final report police intimation, MLC register which are at Ex.P.1 to 7, 17& 18.
10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Somashekara S/o Late Gangappa was the driver of offending vehicle.
The final report, sketch, Mahazar, IMV establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the actionable negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further Ex.P.9 is the reply notice given by respondent No.2 wherein he admit that Somashekara S/o Late Gangappa was the driver of his vehicle, he was having valid DL and insurance policy of the vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.

In the cross examination of PW-1, he clearly deposed that he was walking by the side of the road which is meant for pedestrian, he denied the suggestion that the accident occurred due to his negligent act.
Nothing worth is elicited from the mouth of PW-1 to probabilistic the fact that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.
As per the final report, there is no allegation against the petitioner.

sentences.text: The final report is filed after thorough investigating, and it is not disputed by the respondents and it has attained the finality.
There is no material on record to disbelieve the version of the petitioner.
Further respondents have not lead their evidence, it shows that they have admitted the actionable negligence and the liability.
12. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary, inpatient record which are at Ex.P.6, 10, 19.
The aforesaid documents shows that the petitioner has sustained grievous head injury in the road accident that is sub dural hematoma.
Petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for 15 days in MVJ Hospital and he has spent Rs.2,41,935/- for his medical expenses as per Ex.P.11.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
13.
Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 15 days.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the medical bills.
Accordingly the wound certificate, discharge summary, inpatient record, and the medical bills issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly he has taken treatment for 15 days, for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.2,41,935/-, I award Rs.20,000/-.

In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,61,935/-
compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
14. The petitioner has not substantiated the established his nature of his work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least one month, he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
15. The petitioner has examined the Neurosurgeon as PW-2.

He deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has physically examined the petitioner and verified the entire medical records,
investigation reports.
He further deposed that petitioner has sustained head injury in the road accident.

He deposed that, as per the neuro psychological assessment report of the petitioner given by Dr.Arpitha and by clinical examination of the petitioner, petitioner has mild disability, cognitive impairment and whole body disability is 26.6% as per Ex.13 & 14.

Evidently nothing worth is elicited from the mouth of PW-2 to disbelieve the accidental injuries and functional disability sustained in the petitioner and as assessed by the PW-2.
16.
The oral testimony of PW-2 corroborates with the wound certificate, discharge summary and medical procedures and medical investigation reports of the petitioner.

Petitioner has not Basant Kumar vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63589495/
4 established the fact that the physical disability is an hurdle for his earning capacity.

sentences.text:
Further more,
the fact of percentage of physical disability is entirely different from the earning capacity.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body functional disability of the petitioner is assessed as 23.8%.

The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident, he has completed 44 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.12.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "14".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows; Rs.16,500/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 14 (Multiplier)
X23.8% (Functional Disability) = Rs.6,59,736/- Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.6,59,736/- as compensation under this head.
Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
17.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.25,000/- under this conventional head.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
18.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.25,000/- as compensation under this head.
19. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1 Towards medical expenses, attendant Rs.2,61,935/-
charges, transportation, nourishing food 2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 16,500/- 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.6,59,736/-
permanent disability 4 pain & sufferings Rs. 25,000/-
5 loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-
20 . Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle and they have failed to establish their contention that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.

Accordingly Respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, Issue No.2 in the negative, Issue No.3 in partly affirmative.

22. Issue No.4: For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.9,88,171/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.

Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest and cost if any before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw entire compensation amount with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020.
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Draw award accordingly.
